comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C1, C65-C70) about seasonal polyphenism phenotype and morphological differences. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with statistically significant differences. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns that intermediate temperatures are needed to test threshold response versus continuous norm of reaction, questioning whether this represents true polyphenism.

Both evaluate functional effects of bursicon knockdown (C5, C22-C27, C75). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive functional data including efficient RNAi and quantitative measurements. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting that 'reduced endocuticle in all relevant dsRNA cases suggests a massive molting defect' that may mask effects on morph transition, suggesting different dsRNA concentrations were needed.

Both evaluate miR-6012 targeting of CcBurs-R (C7, C46-C50, C72). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging solid molecular evidence but noting authors 'did not respond to the major comment regarding environmental induction' and that testing threshold response requires a series of induction conditions, not just one temperature.

Both evaluate functional effects of miR-6012 manipulation (C51-C53, C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with functional experiments showing phenocopy of receptor knockdown. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, applying the same fundamental concern that the study demonstrates tanning regulation rather than true polyphenism since threshold response was not tested.

Both evaluate comparative RNAi phenotypes (C89-C90). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting this strengthens the linear pathway conclusion. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, as these supplementary observations were not specifically challenged, though overall interpretation remains uncertain due to molting defect concerns.

Both evaluate background literature claims (C2, C54-C64, C83-C88). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with accurate citations establishing novelty. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, as background claims were not challenged and novelty is acknowledged, though interpretation of what the study demonstrates (tanning vs. polyphenism) is disputed.

Both evaluate receptor knockdown and rescue experiments (C41-C44, C71, C76). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive RNAi and rescue data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with same concern about strong phenotype reflecting general molting defects rather than specific polyphenism regulation, plus noting 'unresolved point regards the source and target tissue of bursicon signaling.'

Both evaluate molecular characterization of bursicon subunits (C3, C8-C14 in OpenEval; C3-C4, C8-C21 in peer review). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive sequence analysis and phylogenetics. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with editor noting 'solid experiments' and reviewers not raising concerns about bursicon identification itself.

Both evaluate receptor identification and characterization (C6, C28-C31, C35-C36, C78 in OpenEval; broader set including C32-C40 in peer review). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with calcium mobilization assays and specificity data. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with reviewer explicitly stating 'Issues related to the assignment of the receptor used as a bursicon receptor were satisfactorily addressed.'

Both evaluate the overall model and synthesis (C74, C79-C82 in OpenEval; C2, C77, C79-C82 in peer review). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED while noting some aspects remain inferential. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with editor noting 'it is less clear what the upstream regulatory events are' and fundamental concern that study demonstrates tanning regulation rather than true polyphenism.

OpenEval evaluates downstream chitin biosynthesis gene regulation (C45, C71). Peer review R5 includes C45 and C71 among broader receptor knockdown claims. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for establishing signaling hierarchy. Peer review rates the broader set UNCERTAIN due to molting defect concerns, though specific downstream gene expression data not separately challenged.

OpenEval evaluates temperature-dependent expression and RNAi effects (C4, C20-C21). Peer review R2 includes C4, C20-C21 among broader molecular characterization claims. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with qRT-PCR data showing statistical significance. Peer review rates the broader molecular characterization SUPPORTED without specific concerns about temperature regulation data.

OpenEval evaluates regulatory relationships and rescue specificity (C37-C40). Peer review R4 includes these claims among broader receptor characterization. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though mechanism of transcriptional regulation unclear. Peer review rates broader set SUPPORTED, with receptor assignment concerns resolved.

OpenEval evaluates expression patterns across development and tissues (C17-C19, C32-C34). Peer review R4 includes C32-C34 among receptor characterization claims. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes data are descriptive. Peer review rates broader receptor characterization SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates dimer formation evidence (C15-C16). Peer review R2 includes these among broader molecular characterization. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with Western blot data showing heterodimer formation. Peer review rates broader molecular characterization SUPPORTED.

Both address overall model synthesis. OpenEval R13 evaluates comprehensive model (C74, C79-C82) as SUPPORTED while noting inferential aspects. Peer review R11 evaluates novelty claim (C74) as SUPPORTED, acknowledging this 'expands our knowledge' though interpretation as polyphenism regulation is questioned.
